title: Incremental JSON patch recovery for truncated streamed outputs and retry safety
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: Implement a robust recovery and retry policy for streaming structured outputs (JSON and JSON-like payloads) that frequently encounter partial frames, escape/encoding edge cases, and mid-stream truncation. The goal is to provide a predictable compatibility layer for existing SDKs and partners (OpenAI-style chunking, function/tool-calling events) while avoiding silent data corruption and minimizing duplicate tool calls. This ticket covers the design of an incremental JSON-patch approach, deterministic idempotency markers, and a client/server handshake for resuming partial streams.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits deterministic chunk metadata for each stream delta (sequence_id + byte_offset + checksum) where applicable
Client SDKs can resume a stream from a validated offset and reconstruct a well-formed JSON object without manual user intervention
Retry of last N deltas does not cause duplicate external tool/function calls (idempotency enforced)
Compatibility shim converts legacy OpenAI-style 'data: [..]\n' chunks into the new protocol without losing escape info
Integration tests for truncated final chunk scenarios pass (simulated network cutoff and reconnection)
technical_notes: Design a small per-chunk header: {seq:int, offset:int, checksum:hex, patch_type:string} encoded as a short JSON preamble or prefixed binary header depending on transport
Support two patch types initially: 'append' (simple scalar/string concatenation) and 'json-patch' (RFC 6902 style operations) for structured modifications
For text-streamed JSON where model emits partial tokens, the runtime will record boundary-safe offsets at top-level JSON token boundaries when feasible
Use CRC32C for checksum to balance speed vs collision risk; combine with seq+offset for verification
Embed idempotency-token for function/tool calls at the chunk level: token derived from request_id + call_index to allow safe retries at downstream tool adapters
Fallback policy: if checksum/seq mismatch occurs and client cannot resume, server sends a final 'replay' envelope with last stable snapshot state to allow deterministic recovery
Compatibility layer: translate existing 'event: {name:"tool_call",...}' and 'data: [..]' streaming formats into the new chunk envelope on the proxy boundary to avoid forcing SDK upgrades
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define chunk envelope spec and publish design doc (this ticket) - 2 days
Phase 2: Implement server chunk metadata emission in runtime pipeline and add checksum/offset generation - 3 days
Phase 3: Add resume API on control plane: resume_stream(request_id, seq, offset, token) that validates and returns replay snapshot - 4 days
Phase 4: SDK changes: JS + Python client patch to consume envelope, validate checksums, and reconstruct JSON; include high-level helper that returns either 'complete JSON' or 'patches' - 5 days
Phase 5: Proxy compatibility shim that ingests legacy streaming and emits envelope - 3 days
Phase 6: End-to-end test harness and chaos tests for flaky networks - 4 days
test_plan: Unit tests for checksum verification and header parse logic
Property tests for incremental json-patch application (randomized op sequences)
Simulated network truncation tests: cut after random bytes and verify resume API reconstructs correct JSON
Tool-call idempotency tests: ensure duplicate delivery of a retried chunk does not re-trigger side effects
Compatibility regression tests: proxy ingests prior 'data:' streaming and reconstructs identical JSON output
Performance benchmark: measure additional latency and token throughput overhead with chunk metadata enabled (target <1% p99 increase)
Security check: ensure patch metadata cannot be used to inject commands into tooling layer; validate tokens server-side
rollout_plan: Feature gate behind runtime flag 'structured_resume_v1' for initial Canary
Enable in internal staging with SDKs updated to parse envelope
Run 2 weeks of canary traffic covering chat, function-calling, and embeddings flows; monitor reconstruction errors
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% of streaming endpoints; provide rollback to legacy streaming behavior on error
Coordinate with support and docs: publish migration guide and compatibility notes
comments: 2026-03-10 Marco Liang: Initial draft. Added chunk header proposal; need feedback on using CRC32C vs sha1 for checksum. Marking as P1 due to customer-visible corruption cases.

2026-03-11 Priya Banerjee (PM): Focus on function-call idempotency — we've seen duplicated downstream charges in two enterprise customers. Please include token format examples and developer-facing error codes.
2026-03-12 Design review note (Evan Cho): UI/Console should expose 'last stable snapshot' timestamps for debugging replayed streams. Added to follow-up UX ticket DES-217.

2026-03-13 Marco Liang: Implemented server-side header emission prototype on feature branch feat/stream-resume. End-to-end smoke shows successful resume on simulated 1MB stream truncated by 4096 bytes; pushing to CI for coverage.

2026-03-13 QA (Nina Torres): Found edge case where escape sequences inside string values (e.g., '\u2028') split across chunks cause parse failure — adding property test to ensure boundary-splitting escapes are supported.
